terra.problem: It attributes the prophet’s condition to taking God’s word seriously. The verse says it is because of the LORD and His holy words, but does not give that reason.
“Ma’am” and “sir” address the baker by terms other than “baker” or “friend.”
Calling these prophets “the ones who spoke for Him” conflicts with the passage’s statement that the LORD did not speak to them.
“Cookie-sheet-sized guess” does not make a clear comparison to the action in the verse.
The passage says the prophets strengthen the hands of evildoers, but does not say their words are what keep people from turning.
“He doesn’t say it lightly” assigns the LORD a manner of speaking the text does not state.
“It started with them” goes beyond saying ungodliness spread from the prophets throughout the land.
It states broadly that these prophets give no warning, rather than limiting that claim to the message the passage reports.
“They have nothing about sin to say at all” claims more than the passage says about their words.
The verse describes the storm as a whirlwind; it does not say a whirlwind is inside the storm.
“That message turns people around” generalizes the verse’s conditional statement into a guarantee about the effect of the LORD’s message.
